title: Detect whether any value repeats
summary: Check guests at the door against a list of everyone already inside, to catch anyone who comes in twice.
goal: Decide whether any guest number appears twice

mapping.story: Guests at the door, in order

examples.label: Nobody came
examples.explanation: With no guests, nobody can come twice.

ladder.name: Compare every pair
ladder.idea: Compare each guest's number with every guest who arrived later.

ladder.name: Sort, then compare neighbours
ladder.idea: Sort the numbers; any repeat now sits right next to its twin.
ladder.insight: Equal values end up side by side once sorted, so one pass over neighbours replaces all the pairs.

ladder.name: Guest list (a set)
ladder.idea: Keep a set of numbers already inside. Each arrival is one lookup: seen before means a repeat; otherwise add it.
ladder.insight: We only ever ask "has this exact number been seen?". A set answers that in one step, with no sorting.

approaches.name: Guest list (a set)
approaches.summary: Check each number against a set of numbers seen, then add it.

transfer.problem: A library scans returned books one by one. Flag the moment a barcode is scanned a second time.
transfer.explanation: Each scan asks whether this exact barcode has been seen before: keep a set and check each new scan against it.

selfCheck: Checks the set before adding the current number.
Returns False for an empty or one-item list.
Uses one pass, not nested loops.
